overview: The Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act would let schools in the National School Lunch Program, the federal program that pays for low-cost or free school lunches, serve whole milk again. Schools could offer flavored and unflavored whole, reduced-fat, low-fat, fat-free, and lactose-free milk, organic or not, and the Agriculture Department could not stop them from doing so. The fat in milk would not count toward the limit on saturated fat that school meals must meet. Schools would still have to offer milk substitutes to students whose disability restricts their diet, and they would be barred from buying milk produced by a company owned by the Chinese government. As of June 5, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say many children prefer whole milk and are more likely to drink it, and that letting schools serve it would help kids get important nutrients while giving schools and families more choice.
against: Critics say current federal dietary guidelines advise children to drink low-fat or fat-free milk, and that excluding milk fat from saturated fat limits could weaken the nutrition standards for school meals.
